changes.title: The AI review now reads each changed part's whole code before and after, instead of only signatures and summaries.

how.words: The prompt and the digest sent to the model now carry every new, gone and edited part's whole text (with its doc block and comments) before and after, plus the changed files that hold no part, cut to size limits.
Defines the `PartText` record: a part's id with its whole text at the version before and after, either side absent for a new or gone part.
Decides which lines above a part (comments, doc lines, attributes) belong to it, so its text starts at its doc block.
Caps one part's text at 4,000 characters a version.
Caps a piece's texts together at 20,000 characters.
The intent sent to the model gains the `code` (parts' texts) and `files` (changed files no part holds) fields.
Skips files the AI should never read as raw lines: Markdown goes as docs, and lock files, the review store and binaries not at all.
Caps one such file's lines at 2,000 characters.
Caps all such files together at 10,000 characters.

changes.why: The old rule sent only signatures and summaries, so the model could not see what an edit actually does; the commit and docs replace that with all of what changed, to read, so the AI can say what each edit does from its own text.
changes.check: Check that the text extraction picks up the right source range (doc block through last line) and that the character caps really keep requests within the 60,000-character limit.

changes.title: When a review is asked in more than one request, docair makes one last request that merges the duplicate changes the model returned.

how.words: Builds the merge request's input: every change so far by number, with its title, why and what its pieces do.
The prompt for that last request: the model answers which numbered changes are one and the same, as {"same": [[1, 4]]}.
Merges each group into its first change (pieces, sources and disagreements without repeats), and leaves apart and reports any group that names no two changes or one twice.

changes.why: Asked in parts, the same change could come back twice from different requests; the commit and docs add a final small merge request so the review lists each difference once.
changes.check: Check that a bad or overlapping merge answer is safely left apart and reported rather than corrupting the change list.

changes.title: Leftover edits in the review comment are attached to the change they sit next to in the code, instead of all landing in 'other edits'.

how.words: The comment builder now calls the module attachment step and lists each change's same-module edits as 'also, same module' under it, with only the rest as other edits.
For each ungrouped piece, finds the change with the most pieces in a module the piece is in and attaches it there, but only when that change clearly wins; ties and orphans stay other edits.

changes.why: The commit reports other edits dropping from 32 to 4: pieces that belong with a change were showing as unrelated other edits, so they are now grouped by module.
changes.check: Check that a piece is not attached to a change in the same module when it actually belongs to a different change's behaviour.
disagrees: docs/EXPLAIN.md's table now says the prompt asks for every piece in its change, yet the code still leaves unattached pieces as other edits when no change clearly wins by module.

changes.title: The review page reads better: it opens on what was done and why, shows how many of the system's flows changed, and folds each piece's actual code diff under it.

how.words: A new data edge feeding the doc page's slice titles, part of the viewer's reworked presentation of slices.
`intent` now fills the new `code` field of the Intent with the changed parts' whole texts, and `changes_page` passes them into the page's `Changed`.
The `Changed` struct gains a `code` field carrying each changed part's text before and after, comments with it.
A new `Texts` map indexes those part texts by part id for the page.

changes.why: The commit restructures the review view: 'What and why' first headed by the title, then 'How · k of n', the flows with their system-wide count right after the changes, and the code before/after as a folded line diff (docair-8l6.38, 8l6.42, 8l6.43, 8l6.49).
changes.check: The page tests were rewritten to expect the new two-step layout and flow counts; check a review with many pieces and large diffs still renders within the folded code diff's scroll limits.
disagrees: docs/EXPLAIN.md says changed files that hold no part go as their `files` lines, but `intent` still sets `files: Vec::new()` in the text shown, so that part of the doc is not yet visible in this piece.

changes.title: A reviewed change now opens on a "What and why" card — its title, why, what to check — before walking through its pieces.

how.words: `changes_walk` takes an intro and, when a review's change is walked, first pushes a "What and why" step framed on the whole change, then the pieces as "How · k of n".
`review_view` passes the change's title and an intro into `changes_walk`, so each review picture starts on the what-and-why card.
The walk now takes the review's texts and, when a review is present, puts a first step framed on the whole change, headed by the title cut to 70 characters, before the piece steps.
The step card is fed data so the new intro step and the how steps carry their navigation.
The end-to-end test now expects two steps: an intro card with what, why and what to check, then the piece card headed "How · 1 of 1".

changes.why: The commit says a review change opens on "What and why", headed by its title, then "How · k of n" through its pieces (docair-8l6.43).
changes.check: Check that a review change with many pieces still frames the intro card on all of the change's parts, not just the first piece.
